title: A regular sequence at a prime spreads to a principal neighbourhood
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be a prime ideal, and let $r\ge0$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in R$. If their images form a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] in the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], then there exists $g\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that their images form a regular sequence in the principal localization $R[1/g]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

source.place: Tag 061L, lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood, specializing the finite module M to R.

proof.text: For each prefix ideal I_i=(x_1,...,x_i), replace the kernel of multiplication on R/I_i by its inverse image K_i={a in R : x_{i+1}a in I_i}, an ideal of R. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] applied to the finite R-module R, K_i has a finite generating set T_i. This is the same kernel argument as Stacks 061L, performed before passing to the quotient.

source.place: Tag 061L, lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood, proof: finite kernels and common denominator, expressed using colon ideals and the fraction membership criterion

proof.text: For a generator a of K_i, the image of x_{i+1}a belongs to I_i R_p. The regularity assumption [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] therefore gives a/1 in I_i R_p. The ideal-localization membership criterion, directly from the fractions in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], supplies s not in p with sa in I_i. In Lean these are isSMulRegular_quotient_iff_mem_of_smul_mem and IsLocalization.algebraMap_mem_map_algebraMap_iff; Ideal.map_ofList identifies the prefix ideals.

source.place: Tag 061L, lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood, proof: finite kernels and common denominator, expressed using colon ideals and the fraction membership criterion

proof.text: Multiply the finitely many generator denominators for each i to obtain g_i outside p. Each chosen denominator divides g_i, so g_i a belongs to I_i on the generators of K_i. The inverse image of I_i under multiplication by g_i is a submodule; the span characterization extends this assertion to every a in K_i. Take G to be the product of all g_i. It remains outside p, and G a belongs to I_i whenever x_{i+1}a belongs to I_i. Empty products equal 1.

source.place: Tag 061L, lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood, proof: finite kernels and common denominator, expressed using colon ideals and the fraction membership criterion

proof.text: To prove regularity on the localized prefix quotient, write z=a/t in R[1/G]. If (x_{i+1}/1)z lies in I_i R[1/G], the fraction membership criterion of [def-weil-ring-localization-away] gives s a power of G with s x_{i+1} a in I_i. Step 3 applied to sa gives Gsa in I_i. Since Gs is again a power of G, the membership criterion puts a/t in I_i R[1/G]. This proves injectivity on each prefix quotient and hence weak regularity by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

source.place: Tag 061L, lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood, proof: finite kernels and common denominator, expressed using colon ideals and the fraction membership criterion

proof.text: The final ideal I_r R_p is proper by the nonzero-quotient clause of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The fraction membership criterion says its properness is equivalent to I_r being disjoint from R minus p, hence I_r is contained in p. In Lean use IsLocalization.map_algebraMap_ne_top_iff_disjoint for [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 061L, lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood, proof: finite kernels and common denominator, expressed using colon ideals and the fraction membership criterion

proof.text: The powers of G are disjoint from I_r: if G^n belongs to I_r, it belongs to p, so primality and properness force G into p, a contradiction. By the same ideal-localization criterion from [def-weil-ring-localization-away], I_r R[1/G] is proper. Combine this with step 4 to obtain the regular sequence required by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The argument includes an empty sequence, where I_r=0 and G=1.
